**Synopsis:**
The FOMC voted to hold rates at 3.50%–3.75%, with three dissents in favor of a +25bps hike. Fed Chair Warsh delivered deliberately vague messaging — hawkish in tone ("will not waver" on inflation) but non-committal on action — sparking confusion among market participants. Underlying inflation has been reaccelerating (energy, food, AI-driven capex) for over five years above the 2% target. Bond markets reacted by steepening the yield curve: 30-yr yields crossed 5.20% for the first time since mid-2007, signaling eroding Fed credibility. Markets now price ~57% probability of a September hike. Analysts broadly expect a +25bps hike in September barring a labor market collapse or a sharp drop in core inflation.

**Q07. Is the content explicitly bearish on US stock markets?**
Explicit: YES — Yield curve steepening, 30-yr above 5.20% (first time since 2007), eroding Fed credibility, and rising rate hike probability are all classically bearish equity signals. BofA's "Doved and Confused" note explicitly flags credibility risk.
Impact score: **72/100** — Meaningfully bearish: tightening financial conditions, policy uncertainty, elevated long yields pressuring equity valuations, and a hawkish split FOMC. Primary risk to NQ/ES/QQQ/SPY is repricing of the discount rate higher.
